package_info.why_malicious: These versions of the lottie-player package were compromised in a supply chain attack to inject a crypto drainer script. The malicious code prompts website visitors to connect their cryptocurrency wallets and, upon connection, attempts to steal all assets and NFTs by exfiltrating them to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

execution_context.file_location: dist/lottie-player.js (main JavaScript bundle served by npm/CDN)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Injects a fake cryptocurrency wallet connection prompt into the website. When a user interacts and connects their wallet, the script establishes a WebSocket connection to castleservices01[.]com and exfiltrates wallet credentials and authorizes malicious transactions to drain assets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code injects a wallet connection prompt unrelated to the animation functionality of lottie-player and establishes a network connection to a known phishing domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate animation library should not prompt for cryptocurrency wallet connections or communicate with external, unrelated domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate web3 dApps may prompt for wallet connections, but only when expected and with clear user intent.
key_indicators: DOM injection of wallet connect UI
Code unrelated to animation or rendering logic
Obfuscated or minified code block appended to main bundle

attack_chain.action: Malicious lottie-player package is published to npm and distributed via CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Websites unknowingly load the compromised script.

attack_chain.action: When a website imports the malicious lottie-player script, the injected code executes in the browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: Fake wallet connection prompt is displayed to visitors.

attack_chain.action: User interacts with the wallet prompt and connects their wallet.
attack_chain.leads_to: Script establishes a WebSocket connection to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script exfiltrates wallet credentials and authorizes asset transfers to attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's cryptocurrency and NFTs are stolen.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected wallet connection prompts on non-crypto-related sites
WebSocket or HTTP(S) connections to known phishing or drainer domains
DOM injection of wallet connect UI elements by third-party scripts
file_indicators: Obfuscated or appended JavaScript code in dist/lottie-player.js
network_indicators: Other domains associated with crypto drainers or phishing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected wallet connection prompts on websites using lottie-player. Inspect loaded JavaScript bundles for obfuscated or appended code making network requests to suspicious domains (e.g., castleservices01[.]com). Block or alert on WebSocket/HTTP(S) connections to known drainer infrastructure. Use SRI (Subresource Integrity) or pin package versions to known-good releases (e.g., 2.0.4 or 2.0.8).
